defaults.t4: We envision a flourishing and resilient Front Range Bioregion now and for future generations culturing through living relational networks and coordinating through decentralized Commons infrastructure.
defaults.t7: Air quality monitoring, watershed stewardship, soil health programs, fire mitigation landscaping — land and water cared for by the people who live with them.
defaults.t10: Knowing who on the block needs to be checked on and who has skills, tools, or supplies to share. Connected, local relationships so that when something goes wrong, we don
defaults.t12: t have to figure it out alone.
defaults.t15: Community water systems, neighborhood farm exchanges (surplus from one yard to the table next door), distributed tool libraries, shared transportation, clothing swaps, potlucks!
defaults.t18: Community solar arrays, neighborhood microgrids, shared generators, battery co-ops — so when the grid trips, we and our neighbors stay warm.
defaults.t21: Mesh networks and community-held servers and datacenters that work when centralized systems fail.
defaults.t24: A shared sense of home and kinship that runs deeper than the basic fact of proximity. Intergenerational knowledge-sharing and -caring. The feeling that we
defaults.t26: to places and people who are known to us.
defaults.t27: We are attempting in good faith the nearly-impossible but necessary work of weaving our communities back together with the life that sustains us all.
